abyss.purpose: The water. Page and scene ground, the punched holes in the binding margin, and Cesium's globe base and underground colour.

plate.purpose: The form stock and the ground of every readable surface. Painted as a 160px seamless raster whose mean RGB is this exact value.

plate-shade.purpose: The punched binding margin and the scrollbar track: the same stock a shade down, multiply-blended with the same tile.

ink.purpose: Titles, entered values, active rows, the slider's pen mark, the head's double rule, the station mark's outline, the model curve. 9.4:1 on the plate.

ink-soft.purpose: Secondary printed matter: field labels, column heads, subtitles, resting rack rows, chart axis text. 5.0:1.

ink-faint.purpose: Tertiary: rack serials, disabled controls, levels with no data, the dashed placeholder bar. 4.6:1.

rule.purpose: The ruling ink. Every rule, track, tick, control border, selection and focus ring on the plate. It never sets type.

rule-soft.purpose: The field rule inside a block: per-row rulings, block dividers, the resting rack row.

caution.purpose: The reserved ink, rules and marks only. The printed margin rule, the overprint frame, the errata top rule. 3.0:1 on the plate, sound for a rule and disqualifying for text.

caution-ink.purpose: The reserved voice darkened until it carries text on the plate (5.1:1). The overprint's letters and printed caveats.

caution-stamp.purpose: The reserved voice lightened until it carries text on the water (6.4:1). Used only by the frame readout below the floor.

stamp.purpose: Readouts printed directly on the water: body colour, cartouche and scale-bar text, the scale bar's alternating segments.

stamp-soft.purpose: Secondary on the water: cartouche and scale-bar borders, the exaggeration line, the Cesium attribution.

display.purpose: The sheet's own title, one per surface, immediately above the 3px double rule that closes the cast head.

title.purpose: A secondary sheet's head, such as the instrument profile panel. Also the cartouche head's register at 0.6875rem.

label.purpose: Every field label, block head and control legend on the plate. Rack column heads drop to 0.625rem at 0.07em.

stamp.purpose: The smallest printed devices: the overprint, the scale-bar legend, the cartouche head. Tracking rises as size falls.

body.purpose: Citations, QC policy statements, caveats, empty-state instructions. Always the sans face, never the typewriter.

value.purpose: Every measured value, identifier, timestamp and coordinate, carried by the .num class. Tabular figures keep a column of 24 depths a column.

shadows.name: sheet-on-water
shadows.purpose: The only shadow in the system. An offset and blurred cast shadow with a 1px hard contact line, which is how a clipped sheet sits on a surface. Applies to .sheet and nothing else.

shadows.name: punched-hole
shadows.purpose: A 1px inner shade at the top of a binding hole, so the hole reads as punched through the stock rather than printed on it.

shadows.name: margin-rule
shadows.purpose: The printed margin rule down the binding edge. An inset shadow used as a printed rule, not as depth.

motion.name: stamp
motion.purpose: The system's entire motion vocabulary. Applied to background-color, color, border-color and opacity by the .stamp class, so a state commits in two frames and stops. No easing curve exists in this system.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: The stamp is removed entirely under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce. Nothing else animates, so nothing else needs a fallback.

motion.name: time-step
motion.purpose: The dwell per timestep when the time rule is running. The scrub and the camera are the only continuous motion on the surface.

narrative.overview:
A CTD station sheet, printed on manila form stock and clipped over the open water column. The globe is the ocean below the surface, rendered near-black; everything a forecaster reads is printed matter laid on top of it, opaque and square-cut. The surface deliberately refuses the category default for ocean dashboards: no dark-navy glass panels floating over a moving 3D scene, no glowing cyan accents, no rounded cards. A translucent panel over a moving scene is unreadable exactly when a forecaster needs it, and glow spends hue that belongs to the measurement.

The organising discipline is that hue is reserved for the measurement. The plate, the inks and the rulings are all achromatic-warm. The only saturated colour permitted on screen is the data field's own colorbar plus one reserved caution ink. Everything a normal interface would signal with colour is signalled here in rule form instead: a hairline rule means available, a 3px double rule means active, a dashed rule means pending, a half-strength rule means no data. That is not a stylistic tic. The product's own accessibility commitment says colour must never be the sole carrier of meaning, because the colorbar is being read as a measuring instrument, and a state grammar built from rules leaves the whole hue budget to the data.

Density is high and unapologetic. This is an instrument for a desk, not a landing page: 24 depth levels print as 24 ruled rows in one column, and the rack never scrolls internally because the rack is the water column. Type sits between 10px and 17px, tightly ranged, because a form gets its hierarchy from rules and weight rather than from size. Motion is a stamp, not an ease: state commits in 90ms across two frames and stops. The only continuous movement is the camera and the time scrub.
keyCharacteristics: Opaque manila plate (#c4b89a) as a real seamless raster, laid on near-black water (#05080c)
Hue reserved for the measurement; chrome is achromatic-warm plus one caution ink
State carried in rule form (single, doubled, dashed, half-strength), never in hue
Two faces with a meaningful split: the printed form versus the typewriter that filled it in
Square corners everywhere, one shadow, a punched binding margin with a printed margin rule
90ms two-frame stamp for every state commit; no easing anywhere
Every colour-mapped value is accompanied by its number and its provenance

rules.name: The Reserved Hue Rule
rules.body: Hue belongs to the measurement. The plate, the inks and the rulings are achromatic-warm; the only saturated colour on screen is the active field's colorbar plus the reserved caution ink. Base imagery on the globe is pushed to brightness 0.52 / saturation 0.26 / contrast 1.24 for the same reason: land reads as context, never as content.

rules.name: The Three-Value Caution Rule
rules.body: One hue cannot be legible on two grounds. Use #b23a22 for rules and marks, #7e2110 for caution text on the plate, and #e8735a for caution text on the water. Never substitute one for another to save a token.

rules.name: The Rule-Never-Text Rule
rules.body: Process blue draws rules, tracks, ticks, borders and focus rings. It has zero text uses in the build and must keep zero.

rules.name: The Uncoloured Absence Rule
rules.body: Missing data is never coloured. On the globe, land and fill values are written fully transparent and black, so nothing bleeds under them. On the sheet, a level with no data prints n/a at half-strength rule; a level not yet read prints a dot leader on a dashed rule. Pending and missing are different facts and never share a mark.

rules.name: The Typewriter-Is-Entered Rule
rules.body: Courier Prime carries only what was entered: measured values, identifiers, timestamps, coordinates, level counts. Archivo Narrow carries the form itself: labels, heads and printed prose. Prose never takes .num. Audit test: read any paragraph on screen; if it is a sentence, it must be in the sans face.

rules.name: The Two Weights Rule
rules.body: 400 and 700 only, on both faces. The variable axis spans 400 to 700 and the build uses neither end's interior. Do not introduce a 500 or a 600 to soften a label; a form's emphasis is binary.

rules.name: The Tracked-Uppercase Rule
rules.body: Printed matter is uppercase with 0.07em to 0.14em of tracking. The typewriter face never takes tracking, because tabular figures already own their advance width.

rules.name: The Rack-Is-The-Column Rule
rules.body: The bottle rack never scrolls inside itself. All 24 levels print, because the rack is a drawing of the water column and a window onto ten of them is a different object.

rules.name: The Unclipped Attribution Rule
rules.body: Cesium's credit line carries a licensing obligation. Nothing may cover it, and every device near the bottom-right corner is positioned off it.

rules.name: The One Shadow Rule
rules.body: The sheet casts a shadow. Nothing else does. There is no hover lift, no elevated menu, no focus glow.

rules.name: The Box-Over-Water Rule
rules.body: Anything that must be read over the moving scene sits in a bordered box on rgba(5, 8, 12, 0.78) with a 1px --stamp-soft edge. Never set text straight onto the scene, and never make a panel interior translucent.

rules.name: The Guillotine Rule
rules.body: Forms are guillotined, not rounded. border-radius: 0 everywhere. The only exception is a punched hole.

rules.name: The State-Is-Rule-Form Rule
rules.body: State is carried by rule weight and dash, never by hue. Single hairline is available, 3px double is active, dashed is pending, half-strength is no data. This applies to rack rows, the time rule's ticks, the frame readout, disabled controls and the profile chart's two curves alike.

rules.name: The Stamp Rule
rules.body: A form does not ease. State commits in a 90ms transition with steps(2) on background, colour, border and opacity, so a change lands in two frames and stops. No tween, no fade, no spring, and the transition is removed entirely under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce. The only continuous motion on the surface is the camera and the time scrub.

dos: Do reserve saturation for the measurement. Chrome is achromatic-warm plus the reserved caution ink; the field's colorbar is the only saturated thing on screen.
Do carry every state in rule form: 1px available, 3px double active, dashed pending, half-strength absent.
Do set every measured value, identifier and timestamp in Courier Prime via .num, and keep prose in Archivo Narrow.
Do print a number beside every colour-mapped mark. Colour is never the sole carrier of meaning, because the colorbar is being read as an instrument.
Do box anything that must be read over the moving scene: rgba(5, 8, 12, 0.78) on a 1px --stamp-soft border.
Do distinguish pending from missing. A dot leader on a dashed rule is 'not read yet'; n/a on a half-strength rule is 'no data here'.
Do paint the manila raster directly on --plate. Its mean RGB is that token, so it needs no colour wash, and tools/make_paper_tile.py with seed 20260907 regenerates it byte for byte.
Do self-host both faces with font-display: block. The demo runs air-gapped and the form must not reflow mid-read.

Do keep the frame budget part of the design: MSAA at 1 sample, FXAA off, a screen-space error of 4, globe translucency confined to the data rectangle, and at most 10 of the 24 depth slices blended at once (log-spaced in depth, not index, so the thermocline is actually drawn). Measured at 44 FPS median at 1080p on the Intel UHD target.
Do verify a new state grammar against a real render before writing its selector. A dead selector describing a state the render never produces reads as a promise the build cannot keep.
donts: Don't use glow, gradient fills, glass panels or cyan accents on chrome. That is the category default this surface exists to refuse.
Don't set text in --caution (#b23a22) on the plate. At 3.0:1 it is a rule colour. Use --caution-ink on the plate and --caution-stamp on the water.
Don't set type in --rule process blue, at any size.
Don't ease, tween, fade or spring a state change. 90ms, steps(2), done.
Don't colour missing data. Land and fill values are fully transparent and black; nothing bleeds under them.
Don't round a corner. The only radius in the system is a punched hole.
Don't apply .num to a sentence. The typewriter is what was entered, not what was printed.
Don't add a second shadow, and don't make a panel interior translucent.
Don't substitute a glyph from an icon font for a drawn mark, and don't signal selection with a colour change; add a registration rule instead.
Don't let the bottle rack scroll internally, and don't cover the Cesium attribution.
Don't interpolate the analysis grid for smoothness. Crisp cells state the real resolution; smoothing invents values across coastlines.
